bear: The stock fell about 4% on November 2 as oil prices dropped more than 7%.

bear: The stock dropped about 9% on the day of the report, after already falling 13% in the month before.

Caterpillar can't build machines fast enough to meet demand, which limits how quickly the backlog turns into sales.

briefs.headline: Disney stock inches up as it cuts costs and pays big to hire AI workers
briefs.summary: Disney shares were trading near $113 on October 22, up a bit more than 2% from the week before. New CEO Josh D'Amaro is reshaping the company. Disney is merging its TV and streaming teams, raising prices for Disney+ and Hulu without ads, and cutting more jobs to make more money. Disney also agreed to pay $60 million a year to hire 66 workers from Character.AI, an AI chatbot company that has gone bankrupt (meaning it can't pay its debts), while one research firm lowered its guess for where Disney's stock is headed.
bull: In its last quarterly report, Disney brought in $25.25 billion in sales, up 6.8% from a year earlier, and its profit per share beat what experts expected.
Disney's cost cutting and price increases are meant to help it keep more of the money it makes.
Hiring Character.AI's workers and getting rights to its technology gives Disney more AI know-how under its new CEO's plan.
bear: Research firm Arete lowered its price target (its guess of what the stock should be worth) from $88 to $86, about 24% below where the stock was trading.
Disney will spend about $180 million over three years on the AI workers' pay and bonuses to keep them, right after laying off several hundred of its own staff.
Character.AI has faced lawsuits from families saying its chatbots hurt their teens, and one market expert said investors now want to see real results.
briefs.nextEvent: Disney reports its full-year and fourth-quarter 2026 results on November 17, 2026, before the stock market opens.
